analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 2429-2954), and the PR only changes documentation. The date at line 3 changes, and 14 lines are added around head lines 1287-1300. Those added lines describe how coordinator SSE chunks pass through SendHandle.sendChunk, ChunkBatcher and the session sink. The excerpts I reviewed (MiMo, Flint, Flash-Next, invariants, code map) are unchanged context. The patch adds no code, configuration, key handling, or authorization or attestation logic, so no control changes.

The new text is worth noting for the next pass. It states that ChunkBatcher.enqueue drops a frame when no session sink is bound. It also states that SendHandle and ChunkSender persist across reconnects, so an old request's frame processed after a replacement sink binds still passes the sink check. It further says this does not enforce request-to-session identity. If that description is accurate, a stale frame from a cancelled request could reach a replacement session, which is relevant to TB-002, T-053 and A-001. The frames are encrypted per request, the coordinator is trusted and decrypts hop by hop, and ProviderLoop+Cancellation cancels in-flight requests separately.

I cannot verify that behavior because the source files (ChunkBatcher.swift, CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift, ProviderLoop+Cancellation.swift) are not supplied. The doc describes it as an observed property rather than as a code change. I therefore raise no finding and record the unverified contract here. A reviewer with source access should check whether late frames can cross a session boundary and whether the coordinator discards frames for unknown or cancelled request IDs. The T-041 cache text was not touched by this diff.
